Your namespaces

    Share a namespace

    A ticket is a capability, not a link to a server — see SPEC.md §3.4/§3.6. Anyone holding it syncs this namespace directly with this node; nothing else grants or revokes it. Write is a shared secret with no per-holder revocation (SPEC.md §6 item 12) — everyone who ever holds it can write forever, but nobody can forge or overwrite anyone else's entries, so a Write ticket posted publicly is a real pattern, not a mistake: a public inbox, a dead drop, a graffiti wall anyone can add to. What it needs on the read side is moderation/volume handling, not restriction on the write side — see the Inbox section.

    Join a namespace

    —

    Shared doc

    No schema, no lexicon — plain text at a key everyone with write access shares and edits. Same sync and capability machinery as everything else here, used as a document instead of a typed record. "A Google doc without Google."

    —

    Inbox

    Submit under a fresh, auto-generated key — no coordination needed between submitters, no collisions, nobody can overwrite anyone else's submission or the namespace owner's own records (SPEC.md §3.4's per-author identifier finding). Pair this with a Write QR code posted somewhere public and this is a public drop box, an anonymous tip line, a guestbook — whatever a "write-only-ish" namespace is good for. Read it back with the Inspector below, filtered to this prefix.

    —

    Inspector

    Every raw entry currently synced into a namespace — no per-record-type code, generic across whatever's in there (NodeProfile, a governance Proposal, anything added later). A debugging view, not a feature; see dump_all in namespace.rs.
